  "description": "This is the part of ripgrep that answers the question 'which files should we actually look at?'. As it descends it keeps a running stack of the ignore rules that apply at each level -- rules from .gitignore, .ignore, git's per-repository exclude file, a global git ignore file, custom ignore file names, user glob overrides and file-type selections -- so a rule written in a parent folder still governs files deep inside child folders. It also enforces the practical limits a user asks for: how deep to go, whether to include hidden files, whether to follow symbolic links and how to detect loops, skipping files above a size limit, staying on a single filesystem, and never searching ripgrep's own output stream. Files that survive all of this are handed back one by one, along with any errors met along the way. Alongside the walk it offers a second, incremental mode: instead of traversing everything you can hand it a single path and ask 'would this have been ignored?', and it loads and caches just the ignore files needed to answer.
